source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 4 June 1949, p. 3 ("County and rural council elections: results"); Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1949, p. 7 ("Ulster local elections: nominations"); Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1949, p. 5 ("County and rural council elections: polling"); Derry Journal, 3 June 1949, p. 5 ("Maghera county council division result")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: BNL 4 Jun 1949 p3: 'Londonderry - Maghcra: J. R. Crawford (U.), 1,066; W. Noone (Nat.), 975. (Unionist gain.)'; DYJ 3 Jun 1949 p5 the same figures (electorate 2,159, total poll 2,041).

note: County and rural council elections were polled on 2 June 1949 (Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1949: 'POLLING took place yesterday in the elections for county and rural councils in Northern Ireland'). Maghera was the only Londonderry County Council contest, the outgoing Nationalist William Noone being opposed by the Unionist James R. Crawford; all the other members were returned unopposed and are named in the Londonderry Sentinel's nominations list of 19 May 1949. Noone was the outgoing Nationalist member; the News-Letter of 18 May 1949 called him 'the outgoing member for the Maghera division'.
